claims.text: Rapidly quenched CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will have a more homogeneous atomic distribution than conventionally slow-cooled nanoparticles.
Rapidly quenched CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will exhibit delayed premelting.
Rapidly quenched CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will exhibit a sharper melting transition.
Enhanced configurational entropy suppresses local compositional fluctuations.
Local compositional fluctuations reduce cohesive strength.
Conventional slow cooling permits incipient atomic-scale segregation in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Cooling rate can control the degree of atomic mixing versus segregation while size and atmosphere are held constant.
Rapid quenching maximizes configurational entropy by promoting a uniform atomic distribution.
Chemical segregation creates weak zones with lower local melting barriers.
Weak zones caused by compositional fluctuations produce earlier premelting.
Weak zones caused by compositional fluctuations broaden the premelting or melting transition.
Across particle sizes of 5–20 nm, rapidly quenched particles will have a higher premelting-onset temperature than slow-cooled particles.
Across particle sizes of 5–20 nm, rapidly quenched particles will have a more abrupt melting transition than slow-cooled particles.
The proposed relationship should hold for CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles from 5 to 20 nm under controlled atmospheric conditions.
Substantially different particle sizes, compositions, oxidation states, or applied stresses may alter the proposed relationship.
